title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Silicon (Si, Z=14) is the interval [28.084,28.086]
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Silicon (Si, Z=14) as [28.084,28.086], with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 14, symbol Si, as Silicon. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Silicon as the interval [28.084,28.086]. This interval is the set of atomic-weight values NIST assigns to normal materials. It is not the uncertainty of one weighing. The notes field on this element's rows is blank. Isotope rows in the same file: Si-28 relative atomic mass 27.97692653465(44), isotopic composition 0.92223(19); Si-29 relative atomic mass 28.97649466490(52), isotopic composition 0.04685(8); Si-30 relative atomic mass 29.973770136(23), isotopic composition 0.03092(11). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
